checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Can a malicious P2P peer crash a validator node by sending batch KZG verification request with mismatched array lengths?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Multiple independent defensive layers prevent mismatched-array crashes. (1) VerifyDataColumnSidecar (called via ValidFields) enforces len(Column)==len(KzgCommitments)==len(KzgProofs) and sidecar.Index<NumberOfColumns(128) before any KZG verification is invoked. (2) VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs constructs all four arrays (commitments, indices, cells, proofs) by iterating a single loop over sidecar.Column and appending sidecar.Index as a scalar, guaranteeing equal-length output by construction. (3) The c-kzg-4844 Go wrapper explicitly checks length equality before calling the C library and returns ErrBadArgs (not panic) if mismatched. (4) The C library itself checks cell_index < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB and returns C_KZG_BADARGS on violation.
state_anomalies_found: NOMINAL: The batch verifier (verifyKzgBatch) aggregates sidecars from multiple concurrent P2P peers and broadcasts a single error to ALL waiting verifiers. A genuine verification failure from one peer's malformed sidecar causes all peers' requests to fall back to unbatched validation via validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg. This is a DoS latency amplification concern, not a crash or bypass.

NOMINAL: validateWithKzgBatchVerifier has a fallback path: if batch verification fails for any reason, it calls validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg which calls VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs directly. This fallback is also safe because VerifyDataColumnSidecar was already called earlier in validateDataColumn before KZG verification.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: The kzgVerifierRoutine drains kzgChan and batches all pending entries into a single batch via verifyKzgBatch. All goroutines block on their individual resChan. The four arrays passed to VerifyCellKZGProofBatch are constructed locally within a single goroutine in VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs with no shared mutable state. No race condition exists.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Attack path trace: P2P gossip -> validateDataColumn -> verifier.ValidFields() -> VerifyDataColumnSidecar. VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks: (a) sidecar.Index >= numberOfColumns -> ErrIndexTooLarge (REJECT), (b) len(KzgCommitments)==0 -> ErrNoKzgCommitments (REJECT), (c) len(Column)!=len(KzgCommitments) || len(Column)!=len(KzgProofs) -> ErrMismatchLength (REJECT). The mismatch check happens at ValidFields, BEFORE validateWithKzgBatchVerifier is ever invoked. No path exists to reach VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs with mismatched arrays.
attack_scenarios: BLOCKED: Attacker sends gossip sidecar with len(Column)!=len(KzgCommitments). Blocked at ValidFields -> VerifyDataColumnSidecar -> ErrMismatchLength -> ValidationReject.
BLOCKED: Attacker sends ByRoot/ByRange RPC sidecar with mismatched arrays. Blocked at verifyByRootDataColumnSidecars -> verifier.ValidFields() -> VerifyDataColumnSidecar -> ErrMismatchLength.

BLOCKED: Attacker tries to trigger mismatched arrays in verifyKzgBatch via batch poisoning. Even if one sidecar fails batch KZG verification, the fallback validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg is safe because each sidecar already passed ValidFields individually before being enqueued.
BLOCKED: Attacker tries to reach VerifyCellKZGProofBatch directly with len(commitmentsBytes)!=len(cells). The c-kzg-4844 Go bindings check this and return ErrBadArgs (not panic).
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: The batch verifier creates a time window where multiple peer sidecars are aggregated before verification. An attacker cannot exploit this window to bypass validation because each sidecar was individually validated (ValidFields) before being enqueued. Batch poisoning causes latency, not a crash or security bypass.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: All P2P-attacker-reachable entry points (gossip, ByRange RPC, ByRoot RPC, initial sync) invoke ValidFields (which calls VerifyDataColumnSidecar) as the first validation step, before any KZG verification.
entry_points: ByRange RPC: FetchDataColumnSidecars -> verifyByRootDataColumnSidecars -> verifier.ValidFields() -> verifier.SidecarKzgProofVerified()
ByRoot RPC: FetchDataColumnSidecars -> verifyByRootDataColumnSidecars -> verifier.ValidFields() -> verifier.SidecarKzgProofVerified()

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant (array length equality before KZG array access): Proven to hold. VerifyDataColumnSidecar enforces len(Column)==len(KzgCommitments)==len(KzgProofs). VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs constructs all four output arrays by iterating a single dimension, guaranteeing equal length by construction. The c-kzg-4844 Go wrapper adds a third check. All three checks are in the call chain.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Primary: VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks len(Column)==len(KzgCommitments)==len(KzgProofs). Secondary: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs construction invariant. Tertiary: c-kzg-4844 Go binding length check.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Guards are sufficient and redundant. The primary guard prevents malformed data from reaching KZG verification. Even if absent, the construction invariant in VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs guarantees length equality. Even if both were absent, the Go binding guard would prevent panics—returning ErrBadArgs handled correctly.
edge_cases: Batch poisoning: One attacker-controlled invalid sidecar per slot can force all legitimate peers' verifications to use the slower unbatched path (validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg). This is a DoS latency amplification informational finding, not a crash or security bypass.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: No vulnerability exists. A crafted sidecar with mismatched array lengths is rejected by VerifyDataColumnSidecar (ErrMismatchLength) at the ValidFields check, before any KZG verification is ever invoked. Even if this check were bypassed, the c-kzg-4844 Go bindings return ErrBadArgs (not panic) on mismatched lengths. The crash scenario described in the checklist does not materialize under any reachable code path.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Informational: Consider adding a comment in VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs clarifying that equal-length arrays are guaranteed by construction after VerifyDataColumnSidecar passes. Consider adding metrics/logging when the unbatched fallback is triggered to identify misbehaving peers.

audit_items.reasoning: Three independent guards prevent the crash: (1) VerifyDataColumnSidecar rejects mismatched arrays before KZG verification; (2) the construction in VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs guarantees equal-length arrays by design; (3) the c-kzg-4844 Go bindings return ErrBadArgs (not panic) for mismatched lengths. No code path allows a P2P attacker to reach VerifyCellKZGProofBatch with mismatched arrays.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Does verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch validate array lengths BEFORE performing any cryptographic operations or array access?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Validation order is correct and enforced at multiple layers. At the application layer: VerifyDataColumnSidecar (called via ValidFields in validateDataColumn) checks array length equality BEFORE any cryptographic operations. VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs's construction invariant ensures equal-length arrays by design. At the CGO layer: the c-kzg-4844 Go bindings check array length equality BEFORE calling the C library. At the C layer: the C library checks cell_index bounds BEFORE accessing roots_brp arrays. No validation-order inversion exists on any code path.
state_anomalies_found: NOMINAL: The Go wrapper kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch does NOT itself check array lengths before the loop 'for i := range cells { ckzgCells[i] = ckzg4844.Cell(cells[i]) }'. However, this loop is safe because all four arrays are guaranteed equal-length by construction before they reach this function. The c-kzg-4844 bindings check lengths before calling the C library.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Symbolic trace of validation order: (1) validateDataColumn receives P2P message; (2) verifier.ValidFields() -> VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks: Index < NumberOfColumns, KzgCommitments not empty, len(Column)==len(KzgCommitments)==len(KzgProofs) — ALL BEFORE KZG; (3) Only after ValidFields passes does validateWithKzgBatchVerifier -> verifyKzgBatch -> VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs -> kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch -> ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch (C library) get invoked. The c-kzg-4844 Go wrapper (main.go) at line 508 checks: 'if len(commitmentsBytes) != len(cells) || len(cellIndices) != len(cells) || len(proofsBytes) != len(cells) { return false, ErrBadArgs }' — BEFORE any C call.
attack_scenarios: BLOCKED: Attacker crafts sidecar with mismatched arrays. Blocked at ValidFields (step 2) before any cryptographic operation.

BLOCKED: Attacker tries to use zip-like behavior to silently truncate. Go's 'for i := range array' with explicit indexing into other arrays would panic on out-of-bounds, but this scenario cannot be reached with mismatched arrays because ValidFields rejects first.
NOT APPLICABLE: The code does not use zip semantics; it uses equal-rate appending to build all four arrays simultaneously from a single loop dimension.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The validation order property is satisfied for all entry points. The Go wrapper kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch does not explicitly check length equality, but this is immaterial because: (a) the input arrays are guaranteed equal-length by construction in VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs, and (b) the c-kzg-4844 Go bindings check length equality before the C call.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Pre-condition invariant (validation before array access): Proven to hold. VerifyDataColumnSidecar (ValidFields) is called before any KZG verification at all reachable entry points. The c-kzg-4844 Go bindings check length equality before the C library call. The C library checks cell_index bounds before accessing roots_brp. All crypto operations occur after all validation.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: VerifyDataColumnSidecar in ValidFields; c-kzg-4844 Go binding length check; C library cell_index bounds check.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. Multiple redundant layers enforce the invariant. No validation order inversion exists.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The validation order invariant is correctly implemented. VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks array length equality before any KZG verification. The c-kzg-4844 Go bindings check array length equality before the C library call. No validation-order vulnerability exists.

audit_items.reasoning: Array length validation occurs at ValidFields (application layer) before KZG verification is attempted, and again at the c-kzg-4844 Go binding layer before the C library call. The validation order is correct and cannot be bypassed via P2P inputs.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Is each cell_index validated to be strictly less than CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB before use in coset_for_cell or coset_shift_for_cell?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The cell_index passed to VerifyCellKZGProofBatch is sidecar.Index (the column index, range 0..NumberOfColumns-1 = 0..127). VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks sidecar.Index < NumberOfColumns (128) before any KZG verification. CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB is 128 in the fulu mainnet configuration (2 * CellsPerBlob = 2 * 64 = 128). NumberOfColumns == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB == 128. Therefore, the check sidecar.Index < 128 is numerically equivalent to cell_index < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. The primary guard (VerifyDataColumnSidecar) correctly enforces the required invariant for all P2P-reachable paths. The C library adds a redundant check: verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch returns C_KZG_BADARGS if any cell_indices[i] >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, without accessing roots_brp.
state_anomalies_found: INFORMATIONAL: The code uses sidecar.Index (column index semantic) as the cell_index parameter in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (cell-in-extended-blob semantic). These are numerically identical ranges (0..127) in fulu mainnet, making the bounds check correct despite the semantic difference.

INFORMATIONAL: If a hypothetical non-mainnet configuration had NumberOfColumns != CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, the primary bounds check would be wrong. However, the C library would still catch out-of-range cell_indices and return C_KZG_BADARGS (not crash).

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Trace for CHK-0108: (1) Attacker crafts sidecar with sidecar.Index = 128 (= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB = NumberOfColumns). (2) validateDataColumn -> verifier.ValidFields() -> VerifyDataColumnSidecar: 'if sidecar.Index >= numberOfColumns { return ErrIndexTooLarge }' — 128 >= 128 is TRUE -> ErrIndexTooLarge -> ValidationReject. Attack blocked before ValidFields returns. (3) Even if somehow passed: sidecar.Index=128 is appended to indices array in VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs, then passed to c-kzg-4844 Go wrapper which passes to C library. C library: 'if (cell_indices[i] >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB) return C_KZG_BADARGS' -> error returned -> Go error propagated -> ValidationReject (not crash). For sidecar.Index = 0xFFFFFFFF: same result — ErrIndexTooLarge at step 2.
attack_scenarios: BLOCKED: sidecar.Index = 128 (CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB). Blocked at VerifyDataColumnSidecar: ErrIndexTooLarge.
BLOCKED: sidecar.Index = 129. Blocked at VerifyDataColumnSidecar: ErrIndexTooLarge.
BLOCKED: sidecar.Index = 0xFFFFFFFF. Blocked at VerifyDataColumnSidecar: ErrIndexTooLarge.
BLOCKED: Even if primary check bypassed, C library returns C_KZG_BADARGS without accessing roots_brp.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: VerifyDataColumnSidecar is called via ValidFields at all P2P-attacker-reachable entry points (gossip, ByRange, ByRoot, initial sync). There is no alternate path to VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs that bypasses VerifyDataColumnSidecar for attacker-controlled P2P inputs.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant (cell_index < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB before coset array access): Proven to hold. VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks sidecar.Index < NumberOfColumns (128). NumberOfColumns == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB == 128 in fulu mainnet. All cell_indices reaching verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch are sidecar.Index values that passed this check. The C library redundantly checks the same bound.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Primary: VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks sidecar.Index < NumberOfColumns(128) == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB(128). Secondary: C library verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch checks cell_indices[i] >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB -> C_KZG_BADARGS.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. The primary guard prevents out-of-bounds cell_indices from reaching the C library. The secondary guard provides additional safety without relying on Go-layer validation.
edge_cases: Semantic mismatch (sidecar.Index as cell_index): Column index range (0..NumberOfColumns-1=0..127) equals cell_index range (0..CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB-1=0..127) in fulu mainnet. The bound check is numerically correct.

Non-mainnet config risk: If NumberOfColumns < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB in a hypothetical config, the primary check would be more restrictive than needed (safe). If NumberOfColumns > CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, the primary check would be insufficient, but the C library would catch it.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: No vulnerability exists. VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks sidecar.Index < NumberOfColumns(128) == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB before any KZG verification. The C library also independently validates cell_index bounds. No out-of-bounds access to roots_brp can occur via P2P inputs.

audit_items.reasoning: VerifyDataColumnSidecar enforces sidecar.Index < 128 (= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB) at the ValidFields check before any KZG verification. The C library adds a redundant check and returns C_KZG_BADARGS (not crash) for out-of-range cell_index. No path allows a P2P attacker to trigger out-of-bounds access in coset_for_cell or coset_shift_for_cell.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Does P2P gossip validation layer reject data column sidecars with cell_index >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB before reaching verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The P2P gossip validation layer DOES reject sidecars with sidecar.Index >= NumberOfColumns(128) == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, before they can reach verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch. The validation occurs at validateDataColumn -> verifier.ValidFields() -> VerifyDataColumnSidecar: 'if sidecar.Index >= numberOfColumns { return ErrIndexTooLarge }' -> ValidationReject. This is the FIRST check after sidecar deserialization. The defense-in-depth question is answered: both P2P layer and C library validate the bound.
state_anomalies_found: NOMINAL: The P2P layer validates cell_index (as sidecar.Index) at ValidFields, which is the first validation step after deserialization. The C library adds redundant validation. Defense-in-depth is present.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Full gossip path trace: (1) P2P peer sends DataColumnSidecar with Index=128 via libp2p pubsub. (2) validateDataColumn receives the message. (3) decodePubsubMessage decodes to *eth.DataColumnSidecar. (4) blocks.NewRODataColumn(dcsc) creates RODataColumn — no index bounds check at this step. (5) newColumnsVerifier creates verifier with GossipDataColumnSidecarRequirements. (6) verifier.ValidFields() calls VerifyDataColumnSidecar: 'sidecar.Index(128) >= numberOfColumns(128)' is TRUE -> return ErrIndexTooLarge -> columnErrBuilder wraps error -> ValidFields returns error -> validateDataColumn returns (ValidationReject, err). Attack fully blocked at step 6. validateWithKzgBatchVerifier is never called.
attack_scenarios: BLOCKED: Attacker sends gossip sidecar with Index=128. Blocked at ValidFields step with ErrIndexTooLarge -> ValidationReject. VerifyCellKZGProofBatch never reached.
BLOCKED: Attacker sends gossip sidecar with Index=0xFFFF. Same result.

BLOCKED: Attacker tries raw byte injection to deserialize Index>127 via SSZ. SSZ deserialization enforces uint64 type bounds (no overflow), and the Index field is then checked by VerifyDataColumnSidecar.

INVESTIGATION: Can an attacker send a sidecar to ByRange/ByRoot RPC paths with a large Index, bypassing gossip validation? Answer: No. ByRange/ByRoot paths also call verifier.ValidFields() as the first requirement in ByRangeRequestDataColumnSidecarRequirements and ByRootRequestDataColumnSidecarRequirements.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The P2P gossip layer validates sidecar.Index < 128 at ValidFields before any KZG operation. The RPC paths (ByRange, ByRoot) also call ValidFields first. No bypass exists for attacker-controlled P2P inputs.
entry_points: ByRange RPC: verifyByRootDataColumnSidecars -> verifier.ValidFields() [VALIDATES INDEX < 128] -> verifier.SidecarKzgProofVerified()
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.defense_in_depth: P2P layer (VerifyDataColumnSidecar via ValidFields) + C library (verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch cell_index check). Both present.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant (P2P layer rejects Index >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB before KZG): Proven to hold. ValidFields is the first validation requirement in GossipDataColumnSidecarRequirements, ByRangeRequestDataColumnSidecarRequirements, and ByRootRequestDataColumnSidecarRequirements. VerifyDataColumnSidecar enforces Index < NumberOfColumns(128) == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. All paths from P2P inputs to KZG verification pass through this check.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: ValidFields is requirement index 0 (first) in all DataColumnSidecar requirement lists. VerifyDataColumnSidecar is called within ValidFields.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. No bypass path exists for P2P inputs.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The P2P gossip validation layer does correctly reject sidecars with sidecar.Index >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB before reaching verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch. The validation occurs at ValidFields (first requirement) via VerifyDataColumnSidecar. Defense-in-depth is present with the C library also checking bounds.

audit_items.reasoning: ValidFields is the first validation requirement applied to all data column sidecars from P2P sources (gossip, ByRange, ByRoot). VerifyDataColumnSidecar within ValidFields rejects sidecar.Index >= NumberOfColumns(128) == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. The rejection occurs before validateWithKzgBatchVerifier or VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs is ever called.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Can a malicious P2P peer crash a validator node by sending data column sidecar with out-of-bounds cell_index?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: A P2P peer CANNOT crash the validator node by sending a data column sidecar with out-of-bounds cell_index (sidecar.Index >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB). Three independent defensive layers prevent this crash: (1) VerifyDataColumnSidecar at ValidFields: 'if sidecar.Index >= numberOfColumns { return ErrIndexTooLarge }' -> ValidationReject, no KZG operation performed. (2) Even if layer 1 were bypassed: the c-kzg-4844 Go wrapper checks length equality before calling C. (3) Even if layers 1 and 2 were bypassed: the C library verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch at eip7594.c checks 'if (cell_indices[i] >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB) return C_KZG_BADARGS' — returns an error code, not a crash, segfault, or undefined behavior. Go's CGO safely propagates the error. The coset_for_cell and coset_shift_for_cell out-of-bounds access described in the checklist cannot occur.
state_anomalies_found: NOMINAL: Batch poisoning DoS: A malicious peer can send a valid-looking sidecar with genuinely invalid KZG proof (but valid Index and array lengths). This would pass ValidFields but fail batch KZG verification, causing all other peers' verifications in the same batch to fall back to unbatched mode. This is an efficiency DoS (extra latency) but not a crash.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Concrete crash attempt trace for all test vectors specified in CHK-0110: (a) cell_index = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB = 128: VerifyDataColumnSidecar rejects with ErrIndexTooLarge at ValidFields -> ValidationReject. Crash: NO. (b) cell_index = 129: Same result. Crash: NO. (c) cell_index = 2 * CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB = 256: Same result. Crash: NO. (d) cell_index = 0xFFFFFFFF: 0xFFFFFFFF >= 128 -> ErrIndexTooLarge -> ValidationReject. Crash: NO. Even bypassing layer 1: C library returns C_KZG_BADARGS -> Go error -> validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg returns ValidationReject. Crash: NO.
attack_scenarios: BLOCKED: cell_index = 128 (CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB). Blocked at ValidFields -> ErrIndexTooLarge -> ValidationReject. No crash.
BLOCKED: cell_index = 129. Same result. No crash.
BLOCKED: cell_index = 256 (2x boundary). Same result. No crash.
BLOCKED: cell_index = 0xFFFFFFFF (max uint32). Same result. No crash.
BLOCKED: cell_index = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF (max uint64). Same result. No crash.
SECONDARY BLOCK: Even if ValidFields bypassed, C library returns C_KZG_BADARGS (no segfault, no crash) -> Go error propagated -> ValidationReject.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The crash path requires reaching coset_for_cell or coset_shift_for_cell in the C library with an out-of-bounds cell_index. This requires: (1) bypassing VerifyDataColumnSidecar's Index bounds check, AND (2) bypassing the C library's own cell_index bounds check (which returns C_KZG_BADARGS before accessing roots_brp). Both conditions are independently impossible to satisfy from P2P inputs.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant (no out-of-bounds roots_brp access via P2P inputs): Proven to hold. The C library's own bounds check (cell_indices[i] >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB -> C_KZG_BADARGS) prevents roots_brp out-of-bounds access even without the Go-layer checks. With the Go-layer checks (VerifyDataColumnSidecar), the C library never receives out-of-range cell_indices from P2P inputs.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Layer 1: VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks sidecar.Index < NumberOfColumns(128). Layer 2: c-kzg-4844 Go binding length checks. Layer 3: C library verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch cell_index bounds check.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient at all three layers independently. No crash is possible via P2P-controlled inputs.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: No crash is possible. (1) VerifyDataColumnSidecar rejects sidecar.Index >= 128 with ErrIndexTooLarge before any KZG verification, returning ValidationReject. (2) Even if this check were absent, the C library verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch checks cell_index bounds and returns C_KZG_BADARGS (not crash/segfault/undefined behavior) for out-of-range values. The out-of-bounds roots_brp access described in the checklist cannot occur on any reachable code path.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.minor_finding: Batch poisoning DoS: A malicious peer can cause legitimate peers' KZG verifications to fall back to unbatched mode (extra latency) by sending one invalid-but-structurally-valid sidecar per slot. This is informational — not a crash, not a security bypass, and the node continues operating correctly.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.severity_estimate: Not a vulnerability (Informational: batch poisoning DoS latency amplification)

audit_items.reasoning: Three independent layers prevent a crash from out-of-bounds cell_index: (1) VerifyDataColumnSidecar rejects sidecar.Index >= 128 before KZG verification; (2) c-kzg-4844 Go bindings perform length checks; (3) C library verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch checks cell_index < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB and returns C_KZG_BADARGS (not crash) for violations. A malicious P2P peer cannot crash the validator node via this vector. The only finding of interest is the batch poisoning DoS latency amplification pattern (informational).
